newsitem.title: USA: North America bunkers steady in post-holiday trade.
newsitem.headline: North America bunkers steady in post-holiday trade.

text.p: North American bunker prices were steady to lower Thursday following the New Years Day holiday on Wednesday, with action still subdued given the lack of players, traders said.
Traders hoped the action might pick up on Friday, and if not, said more players would surely populate the market by next week.
In Houston, both 380 CST and 180 CST eased a touch Thursday, with 380 at $116/117 a tonne, and 180 at $115/116.
Prices in New York also eased a touch, with a 380 CST deal heard done at $117 a tonne, and 180 CST pegged at $120/121.
The premium of Norfolk prices over those in New York meanwhile continued to ripen amid unchanged Norfolk values, traders said.
On the West Coast, the story was the same: namely slightly lower prices caused by a lack of players more than anything.

In Los Angeles, bids and offers on 380 CST material widened a bit, as buyers backed down $1 to $116, and sellers boldly asked for $120, traders said. They said 180 CST fuel remained at between $123/125 a tonne.
Seattle markets were too thin to reliably assess.
-- Oliver Ludwig New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1633
